newsitem.title: TOGO: Integration, security top W.African summit agenda.
newsitem.headline: Integration, security top W.African summit agenda.

text.p: Economic integration and security matters, notably the crises in Congo and Sierra Leone, topped the agenda on Monday at a meeting in Togo of the eight states of the West African Economic and Monetary Union (UEMOA).
A draft declaration, agreed by foreign ministers over the weekend, said that the eight were prepared to join a peace-keeping force the United Nations to put together for Congo.
UEOMA supported the effort and was "available to take part in this peace force under the authority of the UN and the OAU (the Organisation of African Unity)", the draft said.
UEMOA groups Togo, Benin, Burkina Faso, Ivory Coast, Mali, Niger, Guinea-Bissau and Senegal.

Supporters of President Pascal Lissouba and his predecessor, Denis Sassou Nguesso, have been fighting each other in Brazzaville since June 5. A truce was called on June 17, but shelling and gunfire was reported on Monday.
The draft statement also urged the summit to "salute the humanitarian action undertaken by France to save human lives".
France evacuated almost 6,000 foreign nationals from Congo but declined to leave its soldiers in the capital to act as a buffer force between the warring sides.
The draft statement demands a return to "constitutional order" in Sierra Leone, which remains tense after a military coup on May 25.
The eight states are part of the Franc Zone and share a common currency, the CFA franc, linked to the French franc.

They are working towards a free trade zone in the sub-region, and one item on the agenda called for a 60 percent cut in the import tariffs due on certain industrial products from within the area in July.
To offset the effect of this on the poorer states, the UEOMA has set up a compensation fund, with money from a levy equivalent to one percent of the value of goods exported.

The leaders may also discuss the setting up of a regional bourse, to be situated in Abidjan, the commercial capital of Ivory Coast. Originally scheduled for July, it is now thought unlikely to make its debut before mid-December.
